entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Supplementary affidavit filed by counsel for the applicants is taken on record.
2. Heard counsel for the applicants, counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 24.02.2020 and the entire proceedings of Case No. 16346 of 2020 (State vs. Nadeem and another), arising out of the Case Crime No. 261 of 2019, under Sections 323, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Anwarganj,
District- Kanpur Nagar, pending before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate-5, Kanpur Nagar.

sentences.text: It is stated that during the pendency of the proceedings, parties have reconciled their differences and a compromise has been entered between them, copy of the compromise deed dated 16.10.2023 has been annexed as Annexure-4 to the affidavit.

Further, proceedings of complaint case no. 2755 of 2018 (Sabina Fatima vs. Nadeem Khan and others) under Section 498A I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, P.S. Kotwali Orai, District- Jalaun instituted by the opposite party no.
2 against the applicants have also been quashed by this Court on the basis of compromise vide order dated 04.04.2024 passed in 482 No. 3605 of 2024 (Nadeem Khan vs. State of U.P. and Another).

sentences.text: 6. It is further submitted by the counsel for the applicants that if the instant criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.
7. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the applicants or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.
He submits that he has no objection if the proceedings are quashed.

8. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

9. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.
